title: React Native: Screen and controls
lead: Use the iOS or Android development build to change a source, compare Player UI, inspect applied settings and try SDK operations. The steps below follow the screen from playback and configuration to command results and events.

blocks.text: Open Player Lab React Native on iOS or Android. The workspace contains source and theme selectors, a video preview, and Settings, APIs, Code and More tabs. In Settings, choose a category and a property to open its editor directly. Apply configuration and Reset draft remain outside the editor. Long function bodies and nested settings scroll within the selected editor. Selecting a group, field, API view or operation opens its content at the top. Typing and switching language or workspace tabs retain the editor position.

blocks.title: Display language
blocks.text: Switch between English and Japanese using the language controls above the selectors. In compact layouts or with larger text, use More. A language change retains applied settings and drafts. This guide uses the English app; SDK identifiers, code and returned data retain their original spelling.

blocks.title: Before opening the screen
blocks.text: Use the generated Expo development build; Expo Go does not include these native Player modules. The iOS bundle identifier and Android package are both com.playerlab.reactnative. The Player license must allow that identifier on the platform being used. Follow the linked setup and repository instructions to generate the host or refresh its copied local configuration.

items.label: Generate and run the Expo development host
Implementation guide: integration, configuration and UI changes

blocks.text: Choose a source and apply a change

blocks.caption: The iOS settings workspace. Select a source property directly; Apply configuration and Reset draft remain outside the editor.
The Android settings workspace uses the same categories and direct property selector, including external WebVTT subtitle inputs.

items: Choose an on-demand sample in Source and start playback in the Player UI. iOS offers HLS and progressive MP4; Android also offers DASH. HLS and DASH are streaming formats that can provide several qualities.

Open Settings, choose Source in Configuration, then choose the property in Setting. Source URLs use HTTP or HTTPS; match Source type to the media. Title, poster URL and start position are optional. Retain the original values for comparison.

Keep the URL, enter 5 in Start offset (seconds), then choose Start in Start offset reference. Select Apply configuration. If Autoplay is off, start playback in the Player UI. Check SourceLoaded in More and the actual starting position.

Open Code to inspect the values sent to the SDK. Apply validates the complete draft and recreates the Player even for a source-only change. Invalid or unchanged settings leave the current Player in place.

Reset draft discards unapplied edits. To undo an applied change, restore the original values and apply them. Selecting a source sample replaces source fields immediately while retaining Player settings.

rows: Apply recreates the Player. Compare whether the new session starts automatically and starts muted. These switches describe startup behavior, not an immediate play or mute command.
Compare the initial position after Apply. Start refers to the beginning of the media or live rewind window; End refers to the end or live edge. SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live.
Compare bufferConfig.audioAndVideo.forwardDuration in applied code. This is a media buffer target, not a guaranteed startup delay. Blank restores the platform default.
Compare adaptationConfig.maxSelectableBitrate and the selected quality on a source with several qualities. Enter bits per second without units or commas; blank removes the cap.

blocks.text: Offsets and buffer durations accept finite decimal seconds. The buffer field permits zero for automatic selection on iOS; Android requires a positive value or blank. Maximum bitrate accepts whole numbers up to the native/JavaScript integer limit, explained in the implementation guide. Initial Player values are Autoplay off, Mute on startup off, and blank buffer/bitrate. Allow DVR controls the app’s rewind helper rather than an SDK creation property.
Compare playback, tracks and Player UI

blocks.caption: The iOS build after enabling an external subtitle with Player.setSubtitleTrack in APIs. A timed cue is visible over the native video.
The Android build with the selected external subtitle displayed. The subtitle is enabled through the Player’s track selection, not by Mark as default alone.

items: Try play, pause and seek in the Player UI. If the source has alternate audio, compare its tracks in the Player menu. Live rewind helpers and the app state line are available in More.
Choose Default, Sports, Live (DVR) or Cinema in Theme. A theme change recreates the Player and reloads the applied source. Compare the controls and UI settings in Code using the same source.

In Settings, choose Source and edit External WebVTT URL, Subtitle label and Subtitle language in turn. WebVTT is timed subtitle text. Match its timing to the media and use a language tag such as en-US.

Select Apply configuration, then choose the label in the Player subtitle menu. Mark as default supplies metadata; it does not enable subtitle display by itself. Play through a timed cue to check the result.
Clear External WebVTT URL and apply to remove the track and its label/language metadata. To finish a theme comparison, restore the previous theme and restore changed Player values separately.

blocks.title: Scrolling inside the Android Player menu
blocks.text: The video is outside the settings ScrollView. Start a swipe inside the video to move a Player menu, or within the editor to scroll its fields. Selecting a setting or API does not require scrolling the whole screen and video.

items.label: UI customization, platform differences and FAQ

blocks.caption: Code in the iOS build displays wrapped applied configuration and Copy code. Pending draft edits are excluded.

items: Open Code after applying a change. Inspect Player, source and UI values together. Retain the output before changing another property to compare the difference.
Edit without applying and switch to Code: the output remains unchanged. Reset draft discards pending edits. Applying a valid change updates both the Player and the exported configuration.
Copy code uses Expo Clipboard. The output uses license placeholders; retain them when sharing the code.
See the implementation guide for the connection to usePlayer, PlayerView and shared UI assets. This output does not enumerate every internal SDK default.

items.label: How the current code applies settings

blocks.text: Edit additional SDK settings and lists

An SDK is the library used to integrate the Player. Its API exposes configuration, commands and events. The basic form provides common options; SDK overrides and the list editors expose further properties from the installed React Native wrapper. A native SDK feature absent from the wrapper cannot be enabled by inventing an extra key.

items: In Settings, select SDK overrides in Configuration. Use Configuration API to search an exact path such as SourceConfig.description, then select Set this API value. Retain the original value and whether an override was present.
Use the displayed type. Lists accept one item per line, maps accept unique name=value pairs, and enumerations use SDK choices. The UI settings category limits the selector to presentation properties.

For arrays, choose Subtitle lists and advertising, select the target list, then use Edit this list and Add list item. Complete its URL, label, language and format. Source and offline subtitle lists are independent.

Select Apply configuration, then inspect Code and the matching playback, menu or event result. SDK overrides take priority over basic fields. Remove an override and apply to restore the basic value or SDK default; applying an enabled empty list clears that array.

blocks.text: Advertising list items need a position and one or more ad sources. A schedule is input to the SDK, not confirmation that an ad tag, service or media is available. Offline operations likewise need downloadable content, storage and any required DRM rights; use a stable content identifier. The implementation guide explains the corresponding configuration objects.
Try callbacks and native UI handlers

blocks.caption: An explicitly enabled network callback body on iOS. The function changes volume and returns the request.

items: In Settings → JavaScript callbacks and native UI handlers, search PlayerConfig.networkConfig.preprocessHttpRequest and select Edit this callback. Read the arguments and required return type before editing.

Enter a function body, enable Allow edited JavaScript execution and Apply. The supplied default returns the request; the callback runs when a matching SDK request occurs. Inspect the event log and any deliberate visible effect.

Network callbacks may return a Promise; synchronous callbacks must return synchronously. Fullscreen and custom-message entries create handler objects rather than plain values. Use the signature and factory requirements shown in the editor.

To stop the experiment, remove the callback and Apply again. If the body changed Player state, restore that state or recreate from the applied configuration. Edited JavaScript runs inside the app without a sandbox; only enable code you trust.

blocks.text: Run commands and inspect state and events

blocks.caption: The Android APIs workspace after running Player.getCurrentTime, showing the submitted call and returned value.

items: Open APIs, choose Operations in API view, then find Player.getCurrentTime in API operation. Choose a time mode and select Run selected API. Read again during playback and compare the returned position, in seconds, with the picture.

Try Player.pause, then choose Player.isPaused in State and select Read state. Restore playback with Player.play in Operations. For a call without a return value, use the resulting state and matching events to check its effect.
Events displays recent SDK payload summaries. Pause event log stops recording; resume it to collect new events. Clear API event log removes the displayed comparison history.

After destroying the Player or to restore applied settings, open API help and select Recreate player after API experiments. Query resource and track identifiers again from the replacement Player or source.

blocks.caption: The iOS event log shows recent SDK events and their payloads. Event recording and API state queries are separate ways to inspect the same session.

blocks.text: You can also search by a method name such as play. An exact match on the final part of an API name appears first, so play puts Player.play at the top. Other matches on Player remain below it.

Some operations are platform-specific even when they appear in the search. In wrapper 1.29, Player.setVideoQuality and its auto option act only on Android; iOS reports a warning and does not select a quality. For iOS, compare the configured bitrate boundary and observed quality instead. In the Lab subtitle input, blank passes undefined to Player.setSubtitleTrack to disable subtitles.

For an offline experiment, initialize the manager for the chosen content identifier, request options and inspect onOptionsAvailable before downloading. onCompleted reports completion; Player.loadOfflineContent loads that stored asset. Cancellation, deletion and license operations affect the selected identifier. Restore or delete experimental downloads deliberately; Player recreation is not an offline-storage reset.

blocks.caption: The Android Cast startup panel after a full restart: savedOptions and startupOptions agree, nativeInitialized is true and pendingRestart is false. This does not show receiver playback.

items: In Settings → SDK overrides, set BitmovinCastManagerOptions.applicationId and messageNamespace as needed. Blank values use the default receiver and namespace. Keep the previous values for restoration.

Select Save Cast options for next launch in Cast startup configuration. This saves the current draft independently of Apply. Fully close and reopen the app; a JavaScript reload or Player recreation does not restart native Cast.

Select Read native Cast startup state. Compare savedOptions, startupOptions, nativeInitialized and pendingRestart. Android reads the native manager’s public getters; iOS reports the options submitted at process launch.

For discovery, connection and receiver playback, use a compatible receiver on the same network. To restore previous options, save those values and fully restart again. Wrapper 1.29’s deprecated BitmovinCastManager.initialize does not apply edited options.
